slots.writingObjective: State as a fact about TextOS that every action is previewed, decided, run, and its result read back.
One sentence for a search result: in TextOS an action is previewed, approved, then run, and a finished job is not taken as proof that anything was published.

Open on the reader's situation: they asked a tool to do something on their site, and now they cannot tell whether it is waiting, done, or live. Say that this note follows one action from its first preview to the result someone can check.
slots.buyerIntent: Where is the thing I asked for?

slots.heading: How can I follow an action I started, from its preview through to its result?
slots.writingObjective: Answer directly: each action moves through a preview, a decision, a run, and a result read per job; the preview writes nothing; and a job that finished is never presented as proof that something was published.
slots.buyerIntent: How can I follow an action I started, from its preview through to its result?

slots.heading: Before anything runs: a preview that changes nothing
slots.writingObjective: Explain what the person sees before deciding: the preview stores no sign-off and touches no destination; what is reviewed is the same payload that would be sent, not a simplified rendering; and it is shown as an inert reading view with no links, images or scripts. Say what that changes for someone about to approve a change to their site.
slots.buyerIntent: What exactly am I looking at before I say yes?

slots.writingObjective: Caption the figure of this note in one or two factual sentences, grounded in the evidence it cites.

slots.heading: The decision, and the checks that follow it
slots.writingObjective: Explain that nothing runs until a person approves it in TextOS; that a request interrupted before its decision stays open while a rejection is final; that the conditions are checked again after the decision is recorded and once more when the job runs; and that a page update always requires a human review, no standing permission covers it, and only organization owners and admins may approve one.
slots.buyerIntent: Who can say yes, and what happens after they do?

slots.heading: A finished job is not a published page
slots.writingObjective: Explain that a job completing is not treated as proof of publication; that a destination saying a draft exists only proves it exists, not that its content matches what was approved; and that for a page update only a proven content match counts as success, with the result naming the page and the state that were observed.
slots.buyerIntent: How do I know the change really landed?

slots.heading: When the page goes live, the person published it
slots.writingObjective: Explain that when TextOS later checks a draft it deposited and finds it published, it records that a person published it, and that it claims no match with the published text because the text may have been edited. Say what that means for reading the history of a page.
slots.buyerIntent: Who published it, and is it still what was approved?

slots.heading: What to ask any tool that acts on your site
slots.writingObjective: Give the buyer a short list of questions to put to any vendor, one per sentence, drawn from the mechanisms this note describes. Recommendations only, no claim about TextOS.

slots.heading: Where to go next
slots.writingObjective: Point the reader to the related notes. No claim about TextOS.
